title: ID-JAG to the (mock) AgentCore runtime
lede: The exchange issuer turns the agent's caller token into an ID-JAG (leg 1, RFC 8693). The AgentCore leg's target issuer redeems it (leg 2, RFC 7523) and mints the runtime's access token. The (mock) Bedrock AgentCore runtime runs one tool under the workload identity that token resolves to. The AWS side is a lab simulation: no AWS service is called.

nodes.label: Runner · part of this lab
sub: Holds the Exchange and Redeem specs
Leg 1 at Exchange.TokenURL, leg 2 at Redeem.TokenURL
Calls only allow-listed https hosts, follows no redirect

nodes.label: Exchange issuer · company IdP
sub: RFC 8693: caller token in, ID-JAG out
ID-JAG: aud = Resource, sub = the user, act = the caller

nodes.label: AgentCore target issuer
sub: RFC 7523 jwt-bearer: trusts the exchange issuer only
Checks signature, aud, expiry, client, single-use jti
Mints the runtime token with act and the workload identity

nodes.label: AgentCore runtime · mock
sub: Accepts only access tokens its own issuer minted
Refuses an ID-JAG outright: typ oauth-id-jag+jwt
Runs get_account_summary, names the workload identity

edges.label: ID-JAG · aud = Resource · sub = user · act = caller · 300 s
leg 2: RFC 7523 jwt-bearer · assertion = the ID-JAG
access token · sub = user · act = caller · wid = the workload identity
invoke: Bearer access token from the target issuer
the raw ID-JAG without leg 2: refused (token type)

steps.title: The agent hands its caller token to the runner
steps.what: The company IdP signed the user in and issued the caller token. The runner starts from it: it never sees the user's password or session, only this token.
steps.why: The agent's credential is a token with one audience, not a shared secret.

steps.title: Leg 1: exchange the caller token for an ID-JAG
steps.what: The runner posts an RFC 8693 token exchange to Exchange.TokenURL with its client credentials. Exchange.Resource becomes the aud of the ID-JAG, so it is addressed to the AgentCore leg's target issuer. The ID-JAG names the user as sub and the calling client in act, and lives 300 s.
steps.why: The ID-JAG is a grant for one authorization server to redeem, not an access token for a runtime.

steps.title: Leg 2: redeem it at the AgentCore target issuer
steps.what: The runner posts the ID-JAG as a jwt-bearer assertion to the target issuer, authenticating as the client the ID-JAG names. The target issuer checks signature, trusted issuer, aud, expiry, client binding and that the jti is new, then mints its own access token with act and the workload identity (wid) resolved for that client.
steps.why: The runtime's issuer decides, and it mints its own token. Each jti is single use.

steps.title: The runtime runs the tool under the workload identity
steps.what: The runner invokes the mock AgentCore runtime with the redeemed access token. The runtime verifies it against its own issuer's keys, sees the user as sub and the agent in act, resolves the workload identity, and answers get_account_summary.
steps.why: The runtime logs the workload identity, not a shared service account.

steps.title: What the runtime refuses
steps.what: The caller's original token is refused: it was not minted by the runtime's issuer. The raw ID-JAG is refused too: it is a grant for an issuer to redeem, never an access token for a runtime. The refusal names the check that failed.
steps.why: Both refusals come from the runtime's own answer to a real request, not from a fixed message.
